intro: Grant writers often ask what do grant writers get paid because no official federal salary series exists for this specific role. You must manually research and triangulate data from multiple sources to find a fair market value for your expertise.
tldr: The Bureau of Labor Statistics does not track grant writers as a unique occupation.
Compensation data varies widely between sources like Payscale and Salary.com.
Grant writers spend up to 80% of their time on non-strategic administrative work.
Turnover costs for nonprofits often exceed $40,000 per cycle.
Use internal benchmarking and role-based matching to determine your professional worth.

blocks.text: Why finding out what do grant writers get paid is difficult

The primary challenge is the lack of a standardized job category. The government groups grant writers into broad buckets like technical writers or fundraisers. This makes it hard to find a specific number that reflects your actual daily tasks. You are often forced to look at multiple websites, each with different methodologies. Some sites include commission-based pay in their averages, which distorts the data for salaried professionals.
The costs of manual compensation research

When you spend hours gathering data, you lose time that could go toward proposal drafting. This contributes to the drudgery gap. You are essentially doing extra, unpaid administrative work just to define your own value. This leads to fatigue and burnout. Many writers leave the field after about 16 months because they feel undervalued and overworked. This turnover is expensive for the organizations that employ them.
How to fix your compensation research process

items: Focus on role-based matching instead of just searching for a job title.
Compare your specific duties, such as federal versus foundation grant management.
Look for local salary data from similar organizations in your area.
Use grant management software to centralize your own performance data.
Avoid commission-based pay models as they are discouraged by professional associations.

blocks.text: Using your Mac to analyze compensation data

You can use Excel or Google Sheets to build your own compensation tracker. Create a sheet with columns for company size, grant volume, and reported salary. When you find data points online, copy them into your document. This helps you build a custom benchmark that is more accurate than any single website. Always double-check the source of the data to ensure it is recent and relevant to your sector.

faq.question: Why is there no official salary data for grant writers?
faq.answer: The Bureau of Labor Statistics categorizes grant writers under broader fields like fundraisers or technical writers, so there is no specific federal code for grant writing.

faq.question: Is commission-based pay common for grant writers?
faq.answer: While some organizations may offer it, the Grant Professionals Association explicitly prohibits it due to ethical concerns.
